RE: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial for Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT 23472)
Patient Name: Taylor Lawson
Member ID: W261288012

Group Number: [Group Policy Number]
Reference Number: POC-F781755028-57061
Notice of Denial Date: 2026-08-07
Surgeon: Dr. Marchetti, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

Dear Member Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request submitted by my provider, Dr. Marchetti, MD, for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472). Premera Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alaska denied this request on 2026-08-07, stating that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. 

This request was evaluated under Premera's Medical Policy – 7.01.590 (Shoulder Arthroplasty), effective April 1, 2026. A review of my clinical history demonstrates that I fully satisfy all of the medical necessity criteria outlined in this policy. Below, I have mapped my clinical records directly to each of the policy’s requirements to demonstrate compliance.

### 1. Documented Diagnosis
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:
    • There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following:
      o Degenerative joint disease (DJD)
      o Osteoarthritis (OA)
      o Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
      o Traumatic arthritis
      o Avascular necrosis"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** I have been diagnosed with severe osteoarthritis/degenerative joint disease of the glenohumeral joint. Dr. Marchetti has documented a complete loss of glenohumeral joint space secondary to severe osteoarthritis.

### 2. Pain and Functional Disability Duration
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following:
      o Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration
      o Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** I have experienced 12 months of progressive pain in my shoulder that is unrelieved by rest. This severe pain has caused significant functional disability that interferes with my activities of daily living (ADLs) for far longer than the required 3 months. Specifically, I am unable to reach overhead, cannot dress myself without assistance, and cannot sleep on my affected side.

### 3. Radiographic Evidence
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following:
      o Irregular joint surfaces
      o Glenoid sclerosis
      o Glenoid osteophyte changes
      o Flattened glenoid
      o Cystic changes in the humeral head
      o Joint space narrowing"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** My shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) taken on 2026-06-15—well within the 12 months prior to my proposed surgery date—confirm complete loss of glenohumeral joint space (joint space narrowing), osteophytes (glenoid osteophyte changes), subchondral sclerosis (glenoid sclerosis), and a flattened glenoid. Additionally, a CT scan confirms my rotator cuff is fully intact.

### 4. Trial of Non-Operative Conservative Management
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following:
      o Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics
      o Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** I have tried and failed extensive conservative medical management. I trialed daily oral NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief. Additionally, I received an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-28, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief before my pain returned to its baseline disabling level. This documented conservative management spans 8 months, easily exceeding the 3-month policy requirement.

### 5. Supervised Physical Measures Trial
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional:
      o Physical therapy
      o Activity modification
      o Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** Under the direction of my healthcare team, I completed an 8-week course of supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-03 to 2026-06-28. I completed 18 visits focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening. Despite active participation, my symptoms did not resolve. This 8-week trial is fully documented in the attached physical therapy discharge note and exceeds the policy's 6-week trial requirement.

### 6. Exclusionary Criteria / Clinical Not Medically Necessary List
*   **Policy Requirement:** 
    "Total shoulder, reverse total shoulder, or hemi-arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when ANY of the following are present:
    • Active infection of the joint or active systemic bacteremia
    • Active skin infection or open wound within the planned surgical site
    • Allergy to components of the implant (e.g., cobalt, chromium, stainless steel, titanium, etc.)
    • Deltoid deficiency (e.g., axillary nerve palsy)
    • Inadequate bone stock to support implantation of prosthesis
    • Neuropathic (Charcot) arthropathy of the shoulder
    • Paralytic disorder of the shoulder (e.g., flail shoulder due to irreversible brachial plexus palsy, spinal cord injury)
    • Rapidly progressive neurological disease"
*   **Clinical Evidence:** None of these contraindications are present. Clinical notes establish that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. A CT scan confirms an intact rotator cuff, my cuff strength is clinically intact on exam, and there is no evidence of deltoid deficiency or neuropathic/paralytic disorders.

### Conclusion

I have met every positive medical necessity criterion in Premera's Shoulder Arthroplasty policy:
1. I have a documented diagnosis of advanced shoulder osteoarthritis.
2. My disabling pain and severe ADL restrictions have persisted for 12 months (requirement: >3 months).
3. My radiographs from 2026-06-15 prove joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes, and a flattened glenoid (requirement: within 12 months).
4. I failed an 8-month trial of NSAIDs and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-28 (requirement: >3 months).
5. I completed 8 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy ending on 2026-06-28 (requirement: >6 weeks).
6. I have no medical contraindications.

Because my clinical presentation perfectly aligns with the criteria set forth in Medical Policy – 7.01.590, the requested total shoulder replacement is medically necessary. I request that Premera reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for CPT 23472 immediately so that I may proceed with this much-needed surgery to restore my functional independence.

Please find attached my relevant clinical documentation, including Dr. Marchetti's clinical notes, the radiographic and CT reports from 2026-06-15, and the physical therapy discharge summary.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent matter.

Sincerely,

Taylor Lawson
